newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian G-Bank, BBL have no comment on merger talk.
newsitem.headline: Belgian G-Bank, BBL have no comment on merger talk.

text.p: Top executives of Belgium's Generale Bank and Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL) declined on Tuesday to comment on the idea of a possible merger between the two banks.

Last week, Etienne Davignon, chairman of Generale Bank parent Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB), said the idea of a merger between the two banks was still an attractive business proposition, although such an operation remained blocked by opposition from Dutch Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING).

Speaking on Tuesday at a Management Global Information seminar about the future of Brussels as a financial centre Michel Tilmant, the chief executive officer of BBL since January 1, said he would make no comment about his bank's strategy before the presentation of BBL's 1996 earnings on March 5.
His predecessor, Daniel Cardon, had repeatedly said that BBL was looking for a partner to face the challenge of a single European currency from 1999.

Andre Bergen, member of Generale Bank's management committee, said in reply to a question that his bank's strategy remained to be strongly focused on Europe while keeping a strong presence in other areas, but he declined to comment on Davignon's statement.
